\caption{Full measured data-requirement accounting covers all four loss tolerances and both Gemma 3 students, identified by parameter count. Budgets count supervised training tokens, including reuse; pool sizes count independent supervised tokens, and k means thousands. The largest pool varies the training seed; smaller pools vary the pool draw. Intervals are observed brackets, not confidence intervals. Each method cell reports natural-log distances for the boundary rule and the loss rule, in that order. Zero means compatibility with the interval, including bracket endpoints, and does not verify success. A leading greater-than-or-equal sign marks a distance lower bound for a one-sided interval. Log interval width is the natural log of the upper endpoint divided by the lower endpoint; one-sided log widths are unbounded. Unresolved means no measured interval; none means the rule abstains. Seeds disagree when a tested pool tier has both passing and failing runs. Non-monotone means average loss increases with pool size.}\label{tab:dreq-full}\\
